narrative.overview: The interface is calm and legible on the surface and rigorous underneath. A Tasmanian with no finance background should read which projects are over budget or overdue, who funds them, and follow any figure to its source within seconds. It is a dark slate workspace so the map and its coloured markers carry the signal; colour is functional, never decorative. The one place the auditor raises its voice is accountability. It explicitly rejects the dry-government-website look and the crypto/fintech dark-glass look.
keyCharacteristics: Dark slate workspace; map and markers carry the colour signal.
Colour is encoding, not decoration. Neutrals everywhere else.
High information density, generous within it.
Accountability is allowed to be loud; everything else stays quiet.
Every figure is traceable; estimates are visibly marked as estimates.

rules.name: The Encoding-Only Rule
rules.body: Saturated colour is forbidden as decoration. Every saturated hue on screen must mean something decodable from the legend. If a colour isn't carrying data, it is a neutral.

rules.name: The Contrast Floor Rule
rules.body: Body and muted text must clear 4.5:1 against their surface. Muted #9bb8bc on surface #102329 is the known risk; never drop secondary text below this value for elegance.

rules.name: The Status-Plus-Label Rule
rules.body: Budget state is never encoded by colour alone. A red dot always travels with the word 'Over Budget' and, when flagged, a flag icon.

rules.name: The Numbers-Are-Mono Rule
rules.body: Percentages, dollar variances, and budget-usage readouts render in the mono face so figures align and read as data.

rules.name: The No-Hero Rule
rules.body: Nothing exceeds ~18px. This is a working tracker; a display headline would be the brochure the product refuses to be.

rules.name: The Floats-Over-Map Rule
rules.body: A shadow is permitted only when an element literally floats above the Leaflet canvas (panel, legend, controls). In-flow surfaces stay flat.

dos: Do keep saturated colour strictly for data encoding (status, funder, flag); everything else is slate neutral.
Do pair every status colour with a text label, and every red flag with the flag icon, so meaning survives greyscale and colour blindness.
Do render figures (%, $ variance, budget usage) in the mono face.
Do keep muted text (#9bb8bc) at >=4.5:1 on its surface; bump toward ink if a caption sits on a lighter tone.
Do reserve shadows for elements that float above the map; keep in-flow rows and tiles flat.
Do mark estimated funding splits as estimates, with a path to the source.
donts: Don't build a dry government website: no dense bureaucratic tables, no blue underlined links, no flat hierarchy or portal coldness.
Don't drift into crypto/fintech dark glass: no neon-on-black, no decorative glassmorphism, no gradient text, no trader-dashboard flourishes.
Don't use the generic SaaS look: identical card grids, the big-number hero-metric template, or icon-heading-text cards repeated endlessly.
Don't let motion or gradients bury the figures; motion is feedback, not choreography.
Don't add a display/hero type scale; nothing exceeds ~18px.
Don't nest cards inside cards, or give an in-flow surface its own shadow.
Don't use a colored border-left/border-right stripe as an accent on rows, panels, or callouts.
